# Copilot instructions — ha-2N-intercom

Home Assistant custom integration (HACS, domain `2n_intercom`) for **2N IP intercoms**.
Python, no external runtime requirements, `iot_class: local_push`, quality scale `platinum`.
The whole integration lives in `custom_components/2n_intercom/`. Current version: `manifest.json`
+ `CHANGELOG.md`. Maintainers: `@mastalir1980`, `@savek-cc`.

Claude (the analyst, see below) has its own copy of these rules in `CLAUDE.md`. **When you change project rules, update both files.**
Write code, comments, task updates, commit messages and CHANGELOG entries in English.
Several design docs are in Czech — read them anyway, they hold the rationale.

## Your role: programmer

Work is split between two agents. **Claude** (analyst) investigates, decides the design and writes
Backlog tasks with acceptance criteria and an implementation plan. **You** (Copilot, VS Code agent mode
on Jan's Mac) implement those tasks.

- **Work from a task.** Start with `backlog task <id> --plain`. Tasks assigned to `@copilot` with an
  implementation plan are ready for you. If Jan asks for a code change with no task, ask whether to create one first.
  Tasks assigned to `@copilot-mac` (label `manual-path`) change the pipeline's protected paths and are done only in
  VS Code on Jan's Mac, never by the headless coder on the VM.
- **Follow the plan.** Implement what the description, acceptance criteria and implementation plan say.
  Do not redesign, widen the scope or fix unrelated things on the way — note them in the task's
  implementation notes as follow-ups instead.
- **Stop and ask when the plan does not fit reality** (code differs from the plan, an acceptance criterion
  is untestable, a design decision is missing). Write what you found in the task's implementation notes
  and tell Jan; the task goes back to Claude for analysis. Do not guess a design decision.
- Talk to Jan in Czech in chat; everything written to the repo stays in English.
- **Do not commit or push unless Jan tells you to.**

### Code map — `custom_components/2n_intercom/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `__init__.py` | Entry setup/unload, `PLATFORMS`, services `answer_call` / `hangup_call`, aiohttp session, log-listener lifecycle |
| `api.py` | `TwoNIntercomAPI` — stateless 2N HTTP/RTSP client, error parsing, dual Basic/Digest auth, camera, relays |
| `coordinator.py` | `TwoNIntercomCoordinator` — state cache, log events (`/api/log/subscribe` + `/api/log/pull`), ring/motion, backoff, fallback polling |
| `config_flow.py` | User / reauth / reconfigure / options flows, protocol auto-detection (verified HTTPS → unverified HTTPS → HTTP) |
| `entity.py` | `TwoNIntercomEntity` base class |
| `camera.py` | `MjpegCamera`-based live view + snapshot |
| `binary_sensor.py` | Doorbell, IO inputs, relay-active, motion |
| `switch.py` / `cover.py` | Door / gate relays, auto-detected from `/api/switch/caps` |
| `sensor.py` | SIP registration, call state |
| `diagnostics.py` | Redacted diagnostics |
| `const.py` | Constants and defaults |

## Headless mode (Copilot CLI on Jan's VM)

When you run headless via `tools/coder/` (TASK-23), the orchestrator's prompt applies on top of this file:
nobody can answer questions, so stop with a `.agent-stop` file instead of guessing; you cannot reach Home
Assistant or the intercom, so **do not run `e2e/e2e.sh`** — E2E runs on the Pi as the PR check `e2e-pi` after the
orchestrator pushes; you cannot push (no token) and must not edit `.github/`, `e2e/ci/`, `e2e/scripts/`,
`e2e/run.sh`, `e2e/nightly.sh`, `e2e/e2e.sh`, `e2e/staging/`, `tools/coder/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `backlog/config.yml`
(the patch is rejected). Do not tick criteria or set Done: once the PR checks incl. `e2e-pi` are green the orchestrator
adds one last commit that does it (takes effect when Jan merges; label `manual-close` opts out). Commit your work locally with `TASK-<id>: …` messages.

## Working with the backlog

- Tasks are Backlog.md files in `backlog/tasks/`. Use only the `backlog` CLI (`backlog task list --plain`,
  `backlog task <id> --plain`, `backlog task edit <id> ...`), never hand-edit task files.
  Run `backlog instructions overview`; before starting read `backlog instructions task-execution`,
  before finishing `backlog instructions task-finalization`.
- When you start: status `In Progress`. While working: add implementation notes (what changed, decisions, follow-ups).
- **One task per branch/PR**, branch name `task-<id>-short-slug`.
- New tasks and analysis-only Backlog changes made by Claude ship in separate `backlog-<topic>` PRs from `main`;
  do not expect them in your task branch. Your own task's status/notes/AC updates still belong in your task branch.
- **Backlog and analysis changes go straight to `main`** (Jan's standing instruction): new or updated
  tasks/drafts, analysis notes, `docs/*` findings and helper scripts from an analysis are committed directly
  on `main` and pushed — never left on a feature branch. Use a clean checkout of `main` so Jan's working
  branch is untouched. Code changes still go through task branches and PRs.
- **Respect `dependencies`** in the task frontmatter — do not start a task whose dependencies are not Done.
- When done: tick the acceptance criteria, add a short final summary, set status `Done` (via CLI) —
  only after the full definition of done below, including a green `e2e.sh wip`. Put this in the PR's last commit so
  that the merge closes the task (not for tasks labelled `manual-close`; parent tasks are closed by hand).
- Bugs found by E2E carry type `bug` and label `e2e`; they include the report path and evidence.

## Statuses and versions

- **Statuses (board columns):** To Do → In Progress → **To Test** → Done. *To Test* = merged on `main`, automated
  checks green, waiting for Jan to verify on the real device (criteria that need a ring button, relays, Control4 …;
  label `manual-close`). A task moves from To Test to Done only after Jan's check (he does it, or tells Claude the result).
  Until TASK-36 lands, Claude moves `manual-close` tasks to To Test by hand after the merge.
- **Versions are Backlog milestones** (`v1.5.0`, …). Every user-facing task gets the next open milestone when it is
  created (`-m vX.Y.Z`); pipeline/tooling tasks (`manual-path`, `ci`, `infra`) get none. `backlog milestone list` shows progress.
- **Order of work for the headless coder:** ready tasks of the earliest open milestone first (by version number),
  then later milestones, tasks without a milestone last; inside a group by priority, then task id.
- **PRs merge to `main` continuously.** HACS users install GitHub releases, not `main`, so `main` is the next version
  in preparation. Do not hold PRs back for a release.
- **Closing a version:** all tasks of the milestone are Done (Jan tests the To Test items and runs `e2e.sh relays` once)
  → the task `Release vX.Y.Z` (@copilot) bumps `manifest.json` and writes the user-facing `CHANGELOG.md` section from
  the milestone → Jan merges it and creates the GitHub release/tag → `backlog milestone archive vX.Y.Z`.

## Validation / definition of done — run all of these before calling a task done

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests   # full suite, must stay green
python3 validate.py                              # manifest + HACS compliance
python3 -m py_compile custom_components/2n_intercom/*.py
```

New code comes with unit tests in the style of the existing `tests/test_*.py`.

Unit tests and `validate.py` need **Python 3.12+**; results on older Python do not count.

**E2E** (`e2e/`) runs from Jan's Mac against **staging** HA on a Raspberry Pi (port **8124**) and
a real 2N intercom (fw 3.x). Every new feature gets an E2E test in `e2e/tests/`
("HA says X ⇄ 2N API says X"); anything that physically switches a relay is marked `@pytest.mark.relay`.

```bash
bash e2e/e2e.sh wip      # E2E on the working tree, read-only on the intercom — required before "done"
bash e2e/e2e.sh report   # last result + triage
```

- **Never run `e2e/e2e.sh relays`, `--relays` or `reset-entry`** unless Jan explicitly asks — they open the real door and gate.
- **PR E2E on the Pi (self-hosted runner, TASK-22):** `.github/workflows/e2e-pi.yml` runs `e2e/ci/pr-e2e.sh` on the Pi
  for same-repo PRs by actors in `E2E_PI_ACTORS`; check name `e2e-pi`. Staging is reached only via the root-owned helper
  `e2e/ci/ha2n-staging`; all runs share one staging lock (`e2e/scripts/lock.sh`). Runbook: `e2e/ci/README.md`.
  Changes to `.github/` and `e2e/ci/` always need Jan's review — never weaken the guards, never add `--relays`.
- **Never touch production HA** (port 8123 on the Pi).
- **This repo is public.** Never write host names, user names, LAN IPs, home paths, serial numbers or MACs,
  the exact model/firmware build of the E2E intercom, or anything about Jan's home into tracked files, Backlog
  tasks, commits or PRs. Use neutral terms ("the Pi", "the E2E intercom", "fw 3.x", `<lan-ip>`). Exact local
  details live in `CLAUDE.local.md` (gitignored) when present.
- Never print, copy or commit values from `e2e/.env`.
- If E2E fails, follow `e2e/agent/triage.md`: a failure caused by your change is fixed in the task;
  an unrelated or pre-existing failure goes to Backlog as a bug (type `bug`, label `e2e`) and Jan is told.

Also: docs touched by the change updated (`README.md`, `docs/*`); one task per branch `task-<id>-short-slug`.

## Architecture you must not break

- **Event-driven first.** Real-time state comes from the log channel; polling (default 60 s) is only
  a safety net. Ring detection is **exclusively** event-driven. A log event the device does not
  support must degrade gracefully (see `MotionDetected` in `coordinator.py`) — never let one
  unsupported event break the whole subscription.
- **Dual auth in `api.py` is intentional.** The device configures Basic/Digest **per service group**:
  Digest via `aiohttp.DigestAuthMiddleware(preemptive=False)`, Basic retry on `401 + Basic`.
  **Never "simplify" this to a single scheme.** Basic over plaintext HTTP is refused unless the user
  opted into `allow_insecure`.
- `entity.py` — every platform entity extends `TwoNIntercomEntity`; static properties use `_attr_*`.
- Config: `entry.data` = connection identity, `entry.options` = behaviour. Keep the separation.
- Credentials never appear in URLs, logs, diagnostics, tasks or commits (`diagnostics.py` redacts;
  MJPEG credentials go to `MjpegCamera` separately). Only known exception: the RTSP URL.
- New platform: `<platform>.py`, register in `PLATFORMS` in `__init__.py`, update `strings.json`,
  `translations/en.json`, `translations/de.json`, `translations/cs.json` and `icons.json` together.
- Services follow `answer_call`/`hangup_call` in `__init__.py`: target a config entry, declare in
  `services.yaml`, translate in `strings.json`.

## 2N device specifics

- Endpoints in use: `README.md` ("2N API Endpoints Used") and `docs/API_REFERENCE.md`.
- Call control uses **GET**, not POST. Error code 14 is overloaded — disambiguate by `description`.
- Snapshot resolution must come from `camera/caps`; MJPEG `fps` is valid 1–15.
- RTSP has its own user database, independent of HTTP API accounts.
- Code was validated on IP Verso fw 2.50; the E2E device runs fw 3.x — expect differences
  (e.g. TASK-12, `code 7 "invalid connection type"`). Firmware < 2.40 is out of scope.

## Conventions

- Timestamps tz-aware via `homeassistant.util.dt` — no new naive `datetime.now()`.
- Broad `except Exception` only for intentional, logged degradation; prefer narrow types.
- `manifest.json` version bumps and `CHANGELOG.md` entries belong in release tasks, not in every PR.
- Update user docs (`README.md`, `INSTALLATION.md`) and `docs/*` when behaviour changes.
